tests_notes: Identical and empty strings, classic pairs, symmetry, accented characters; workload: two sentence pairs of about 150 characters.

A.strategy: Two rolling rows, comparisons instead of min
A.rationale: Each cell needs only the previous row, so two lists replace the full table, and two comparisons replace building a list for min() per cell. Same recurrence, same distance.

B.strategy: Bind rows locally, inline the minimum
B.rationale: Keeps the table but reads the current and previous rows through locals and takes the minimum with two comparisons, so each cell avoids four double indexings and a list allocation.

C.rationale: Iterating zip(target, previous, previous[1:]) yields the diagonal and upper cells directly, so the inner loop does no indexing at all.

C.diagnosis: The min( call in the inner loop was never closed. Rewrote that line as explicit comparisons, which also saves a min() call per cell.
C.strategy: Zip over the previous row, compare
C.rationale: zip yields each cell's diagonal and upper neighbours without indexing; the minimum of the three edits is taken with two comparisons. Identical recurrence, two rows of memory.

notes: C first comes back with an unclosed parenthesis (a syntax rejection) and wins after one repair; A and B are both clear wins.
